Thanks again for joining the demo today — great discussion. To get the pilot scoped and to recommend the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC), I need a couple of concrete numbers from your side so we can match performance guarantees and provide a tight estimate. Can you confirm the items below?

Quick ask (one reply):
- Target p95 latency for generation in production (ms) — is 80ms, 150ms, or 300ms the right bucket?
- Expected peak concurrent QPS (requests per second) and typical working set QPS.
- Average prompt + response token count (approx tokens in/out).
- Session/affinity requirements (do you need KV cache pinned to sessions for personalization?)
- Security constraints: SOC2? VPC-only? On-prem?
- Ideal pilot length and go/no-go criteria (e.g., <150ms p95 at 50qps for 2 weeks).

Attached: BrightPilot_QPS_SLA.xlsx (spreadsheet with a sample load profile) and our high-level dedicated estimate. Based on the call, my initial read: if you need sub-100ms p95 at sustained 100+ qps, Dedicated is likely the right path. If you can accept 150-300ms p95 with cost plus simplicity, Hosted API pilot with reserved burst might work for the initial test.

Next steps I propose after you reply:
1) Redwood provides two SKUs: a 2-week Dedicated pilot config + canary fallback, and a Hosted-API premium-route pilot.
2) We run a short load test with your sample prompts (we can host the test harness).
3) We agree pass/fail metrics and SLOs, then move to purchase/order.

Thanks — one-line answers here will unblock the quote.

Thanks Jordan — quick answers below (happy to follow up with details):

- Target p95 latency: goal is 120ms for text generation in the checkout assistant path; our strictest path is product search suggestions where 80-100ms would be ideal but not mandatory for the pilot.
- Expected peak concurrent QPS: peak observed during promo spikes ~150 qps. Typical steady-state ~35-45 qps.
- Avg tokens: prompt ~120 tokens, response ~90 tokens (so ~210 tokens round-trip).
- Session/affinity: yes, we have session-level personalization and would prefer KV cache affinity for active carts (so some sticky cache benefit).
- Security: SOC2 required; data residency must be US-only for this pilot. Private on-prem not required at this stage.
- Pilot length: 3 weeks preferred; go/no-go: maintain p95 <160ms at 40qps and no more than 10% error rate for generation.

We are looping in procurement (Michael) — they will want a formal quote and a statement of work. Also, legal will want a vendor questionnaire and SOC2 evidence.

Thanks Sasha — great data, that's very helpful. Technical read and recommendation below (TL;DR: Dedicated pilot with canary fallback gives the highest probability of meeting the sub-160ms p95 requirement at your peak profiles).

Short technical summary:
- Tokens: ~210 tokens RT means compute per request is non-trivial; at 150 peak qps sustained, continuous batching must be tuned aggressively to hit p95 targets.
- Session affinity: KV cache affinity needed for personalization; Dedicated allows us to pin cache to GPU pools easily (lower miss rate, lower tail latency). Hosted API supports per-customer cache but may introduce higher p95 during burst windows.
- Data residency & SOC2: both supported in Dedicated (US region); we will provide SOC2 report and a KMS integration for keys.

Recommendations (pilot):
1) Provision a small Dedicated pool sized for ~80 sustained qps with autoscale headroom to 160 qps for bursts for 3-week pilot. We'll instrument end-to-end p95 and KV hit rates.
2) Canary fallback: configure a Hosted-API fallback route for non-critical traffic to avoid user-visible errors during autoscale events.
3) Performance targets: primary SLO p95 <160ms at 40qps steady; stretch SLO p95 <120ms at 40qps; verify behavior at 150 qps burst for up to 5 minutes.
4) Run our load test using your prompt corpus; we'll provide a harness and collect traces.

Attached is a preliminary estimate (redwood-dedicated-estimate.pdf). If you prefer, we can also price a Hosted premium-route pilot (lower infra cost but higher risk on tail latency).

Next technical steps:
- Jordan: confirm which pilot SKU you want us to price formally (Dedicated pilot w/ 3-week commitment OR Hosted premium-route pilot).
- Sasha: we'll need test prompt corpus and a sample API key to run the load test (or we can give you an upload link).
- Michael / Procurement: Marissa will send the SOW template and pilot quote once SKU choice is confirmed.
